sections.h2: Which Richmond County offices handle my tax bill?
sections.html:
Valuation and collection sit in different hands here. Appraisers working for the Board of Assessors value each parcel, and the elected Tax Commissioner, whose site is arctax.com, prints the bills and accepts payment. Because the commissioner has no hand in the size of any levy, a dispute over rates belongs with the commission and school board, and a dispute over worth belongs with the appraisers.

  • Assessors: 706-821-2310, plus an online property search.
  • Tax Commissioner: 706-821-2391, counter at 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta.
  • Mail to the commissioner: P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903.

Richmond County is consolidated with Augusta, so county notices appear on the Augusta government website and a single government sits behind the county and city side of the bill.

sections.h2: What do Richmond County's numbers say about its housing?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts, linked here, shows 206,559 residents in July 2025 on 324.34 square miles of land, level with 206,607 counted in 2020. The county has 76,694 households and an estimated 94,651 housing units. Authorities issued 534 building permits in 2025.

Owners hold only 51.2 percent of households, so renters are nearly half. A typical owned home is valued at $178,500 and a typical rent is $1,141. The middle household earns $55,637, 19.0 percent of people live below the poverty line, and 17,087 are veterans. The drive to work averages 21.4 minutes.

With so many rentals, buyers here include landlords as well as first-time owners. A parcel with deferred repairs or an old tax balance sells at a discount, since the buyer subtracts what the county is owed.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 millage rates in Richmond County?
sections.html:
Four net rates are posted for 2026. The tax district that contains the parcel picks the one that applies.

The commissioner's millage page defines a mill as $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value and says the county commission and the school board each add their own rate to the total. Assessed value is 40 percent of market value. Your assessment notice carries an estimated tax savings box, so check it against the final bill.

sections.h2: When does Richmond County collect property tax?
sections.html:
For the 2026 bills, the due dates page lists November 30, with mobile home tax due April 1. Per the assessor FAQ, bills mail in August or September as a rule.

Whatever remains unpaid is charged .875 percent interest monthly (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40), and a single 10 percent penalty follows. If the account keeps sitting, a lien and levy can follow. Settle an old balance ahead of any sale. The commissioner's page stresses that the owner remains responsible for payment, whoever was supposed to remit it.

Escrow does not transfer the legal duty. Lenders do not get paper bills from the office, only the data. After a change of servicer, phone the new company and ask whether the county account was paid.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Richmond County valuation?
sections.html:
The clock is 45 days and starts on the date the notice was mailed. The batch mailed June 29, 2026 had an August 13, 2026 cutoff, which has passed. The next notice states its own date.

You can file through the assessor's website, by post, by email or in person. Since 2011 every owner receives a yearly notice, even when nothing changed. A change in 2026 is the layout: Senate Bill 566 replaced the old tax estimate grid with an estimated savings section plus appeal and exemption directions.

  • Pull sale prices of comparable houses close to yours.
  • Photograph defects that lower value.
  • If the assessors keep their number, the Board of Equalization is next, and Superior Court after it.

sections.h2: What homestead relief does Richmond County offer?
sections.html:
You qualify by living in the house on January 1 and filing by April 1. The commissioner takes the form and sends it to the assessors for a ruling, and an owner who is turned down may go to the Board of Equalization.

After approval the benefit rolls forward by itself. Owners refile only after a deed change in name or spelling, an ownership change, or when they want a different exemption. Refinancing leaves it alone. A couple gets one homestead between them, and each vehicle either spouse owns has to be registered here. Solid waste and street light fees stay payable.

Augusta adds a local floating homestead exemption, aimed at holding back growth in the assessed value of a primary home. The form is accepted from January 1 through the end of the 45 day appeal window that follows the mailing of assessment notices, and it can accompany an appeal or replace one. Each applicant states citizenship or immigration status under O.C.G.A. 50-36-1, and qualified aliens attach their federal documents. Senior and other special exemptions need an in-person or mailed application with full documentation. For mailed forms the office recommends certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are refused.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax in a Richmond County sale?
sections.html:
Georgia puts each year's tax on whoever holds title January 1. A contract can pass that burden to the buyer, which the closing table normally handles. The commissioner will not divide the year between the parties.

  • A bill goes to the January 1 owner and to any buyer who took title later that year.
  • If nobody pays, the lien carries the January 1 owner's name, unless the seller shows the deed plus closing papers inside 90 days of the due date.
  • The office calls its proof an acknowledgment and receipt of settlement statement.

If a fall closing runs on an estimated tax figure, ask the attorney who absorbs any gap when the real bill arrives, and keep your signed settlement statement.

sections.h2: How can I check whether a Richmond County parcel is current?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner publishes a mass tax bill file listing outstanding real estate balances, normally refreshed on Mondays. Its warning is worth repeating: some accounts are coded bankruptcy, under appeal or awaiting an assessment change, and those are not yet due, so a balance in the file does not by itself mean a delinquency.

For an exact status, call 706-821-2391 and have the bill number or map and parcel number ready. Bad checks go to a recovery partner, Envision Payment Solutions, and a service fee applies under state law.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Richmond County house with taxes behind?
sections.html:
Yes. A payoff request goes from the title company to the commissioner, and the amount is deducted from your proceeds the way a mortgage payoff is.

Cash buyers suit inherited and empty houses and parcels where a lien has started to grow, because no repair list or loan approval holds up the closing. Compare any offer with a standard listing minus repairs and holding costs, and call the commissioner for the live balance first.

faqs.q: How many days do Richmond County owners get to appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the notice. The 2026 batch ran out on August 13.

faqs.q: What is the Richmond County homestead filing date?
faqs.a: April 1, for a home you occupied on January 1. After approval, the benefit continues until the deed or the owner changes.

faqs.q: Will the Richmond County tax commissioner split tax between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No. Buyer and seller settle that between themselves at closing, and their papers can later show who took on the tax.

faqs.q: What does a late Richmond County bill cost?
faqs.a: The due dates page posts .875 percent interest per month and one 10 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Where does a mailed Richmond County homestead form go?
faqs.a: To P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903. Use certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are rejected.
